  -- lens, nothing polymorphic. They replace `population_code` (retired by that ruling's
  -- own ACTION) and `population_label`, the free-text companion that had no registry at
  -- all -- retiring the typed column while keeping the untyped one beside it would keep
  -- the exact defect the ruling was issued against.
  --
  -- `base_taxonomy_medical` holds 0 rows today, so a NON-NULL medical_code is
  -- unwritable until it is seeded. That is the CLAUDE.md §4 trap, and it is harmless in
  -- this shape precisely because the column is nullable and the CHECK is "at least one":
  -- the table stays writable through any of the other three. `specifications` carries the
  -- identical arrangement from 071.
  identity_code          TEXT REFERENCES populations(population_code),
  icf_code               TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
  needs_code             TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
  medical_code           TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),

  jurisdiction           TEXT,
  setting                TEXT,

                           CHECK (claim_type IN ('numerical','range','qualitative','framework','absent')),

  claim_text             TEXT,
  source_section         TEXT,

  root_id                TEXT,
  root_type              TEXT

  root_ref_id            TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
  echo_of                TEXT,
  measurement_paradigm   TEXT

  device_class           TEXT

1	# Batch 19 — the pre-1990 chain: Steinfeld's bibliography, Walter, Templer
2	
3	**Assignment:** batch 18 §9 items 1–4, in that order. GAP-025 established that a deferral runs
4	because a batch is told to run it, not because a counter goes red; this is that batch.
5	
6	**Priors:** `scratchpad/<session>/priors.md`, committed **before** the bibliography was transcribed
7	or any screen run. P6 (Co-1) was appended later and says so in its own text.
8	
9	**Derive every figure below.** Nothing here is a count to quote.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1. What the batch was for, and what it actually found
14	
15	Item 1 was the assigned work and it produced the batch's substantive finding, which is **not** the
16	one the assignment anticipated. The assignment expected REF-01005's reference list to be "the index
17	to the whole pre-1990 layer". It is 38 entries of **ergonomics**, and the two items its own
18	recommendation table names as warrants do not behave as the register assumed.
19	
20	## 2. Item 1 — REF-01005 backward, and four predictions
21	
22	No Crossref deposit exists for this report, so there was no reference list to fetch. The 38 entries
23	were transcribed from the persisted ED184280 scan (pypdf page indices 167–169) and persisted as a
24	**derived** artefact. Derive the yield:
25	
26	    python3 scripts/research/mining_screen.py --ref REF-01005 --compare
27	
28	| Prediction | Result |
29	|---|---|
30	| **P1a** ≥ 60 references | **FALSIFIED** — 38 |
31	| **P1b** slope-strict yield 3–12 | **FALSIFIED** — the band is below it |
32	| **P1c** slope-loose ≥ 3× slope-strict | **FALSIFIED** — they are almost the same |
33	| **P1d** Templer and Walter both present as discrete entries | **CONFIRMED**, with a discrepancy worth more than the prediction |
34	
35	**On P1b I must record a second failure, of my own instrument rather than of the prediction.** I
36	pre-registered "falsified if the yield is 0 or ≥ 20". The yield missed the predicted band and **did
37	not trigger my own falsification condition**, because I set that condition far wider than the
38	prediction it was supposed to test. A threshold that cannot fire when the point prediction fails is
39	not a test. Reported here rather than behind the looser rule that let me off.
40	
41	**On P1c the reasoning was wrong in a way worth keeping.** I predicted the bare stem `accessib`
42	would fire on everything because REF-01005 is an accessibility report. It fires on almost nothing:
43	the **bibliography** is a human-factors and ergonomics bibliography — Damon, Diffrient, Kroemer,
44	McCormick, Murrell, Poulton, with *Human Factors* and *Applied Ergonomics* as the recurring venues.
45	A 1979 federal accessibility report drew its authority from ergonomics, not from a disability
46	literature. That is a finding about the period, and it means **a screen's behaviour tracks the
47	literature an anchor cites, not the subject of the anchor itself.**
48	
49	**The most instructive result is a negative one.** Walter's entry scores **zero under every screen**,
50	because its title in this bibliography carries no slope term — *"Part 3: Ramp gradients"* is a part
51	title. The single most slope-relevant item in the list is invisible to a title screen. No later
52	reader should read a low yield here as a thin literature.
53	
54	## 3. Table 13's footnote is narrower than the register records — and this runs against GAP-037
55	
56	GAP-037 clause (4) says Table 13 "rests partly on others" and treats Templer and Walter as the two
57	remaining nodes of **the 1:12 chain**. Reading the table itself:
58	
59	- The footnote marker `c` appears on the **1:8 and 1:10** rows. It does **not** appear on 1:12 or 1:16.
60	- Table 12 shows the study tested exactly **1:12, 1:16 and 1:20**.
61	
62	So the two bands carrying "based on research of others" are **precisely the two outside the tested
63	range**, and the 1:12 and 1:16 rows rest on Steinfeld's own data. On that reading Templer and Walter
64	are not nodes of the 1:12 chain at all, and the priority of retrieving them drops.
65	
66	**Held as a reading, not as settled.** These are single characters on a damaged scan. A cleaner copy
67	of page 57 decides it in one look. Recorded as extraction 56 and as an amendment to GAP-037 rather
68	than as a correction to it.
69	
70	## 4. Item 3 — Templer 1977 does not resolve, and the surname is settled
71	
72	Four indexes, and the negative is well-formed rather than empty (R14):
73	
74	- **ERIC** `author:"Templer"` → 33 records, a healthy set, **none architectural** (Bill Templer,
75	  education; Donald I. Templer, psychology; Andrew J. Templer, management; Lois; Sally).
76	  `"Templer" AND "stairs"` → **0**. A sound query shape returning 33 and a topic conjunction
77	  returning 0 is genuine absence *in ERIC*, which is an education index.
78	- **OpenAlex** Templer + 1977 → 10, none architectural.
79	- **Crossref** on the dissertation title REF-01005 actually lists → **John A. Templer's corpus**:
80	  1974 dissertation *Stair shape and human movement*; 1978 *An analysis of the behavior of stair
81	  users* (NBS IR 78-1554, doi 10.6028/nbs.ir.78-1554); 1984 *The Forgiving Stair*; 1989 *The Soft Stair*.
82	- **TRID** served a 200 whose page carries no extractable record — a JS shell. Nothing is
83	  established about what TRID holds.
84	
85	**Four items across fifteen years, not one about ramps, and nothing dated 1977.** The bibliography's
86	own Templer is the 1974 stairs dissertation, so the report cites a year its own reference list does
87	not carry.
88	
89	**Which item footnote c meant is still not guessed** — batch 18 §9 said it must not be, and the two
90	nearest neighbours (1974 and 1978) straddle it. Candidate 115 called it "the ramp-slope research";
91	that was a guess and it is corrected under R15. Candidate 117 stages the 1978 NBS report as the
92	nearest *resolvable* neighbour, explicitly without claiming it is the referent.
93	
94	**The structural finding survives whichever it is:** footnote c warrants Table 13's steepest bands on
95	two named parties, and one of them has no ramp research to his name.
96	
97	## 5. Item 2 — Walter: the named route is closed, and the holdings layer is what is new
98	
99	**Jisc Library Hub Discover is unreachable from here** — HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare interstitial,
100	twice. Candidate 109 and GAP-037 both named Jisc as the next route; it is closed, and nothing is
101	established about what Jisc holds.
102	
103	**A correction I nearly filed and did not.** I formed the hypothesis that batch 18 had fetched the
104	Open Library record and failed to read it, and checked before writing anything. **It had read it** —
105	Felix Walter, DLF, London, 1971, 60 pp is already correctly in candidate 109, with the
106	corporate-versus-directing-author distinction properly drawn. Nothing is retracted from it. Recording
107	the near-miss because a false accusation against a previous batch would have been cheap to make and
108	hard to unpick.
109	
110	**What is new is the holdings layer:** ISBN-10 0901908053, **LCCN 77502052**, **OCLC 222208**, LC
111	class NA2545.P5 D5, one edition, source record `marc:marc_loc_2016` — a Library of Congress MARC
112	record, which is why the 1971 date is authoritative rather than inferred while the bibliography's own
113	year digits for Walter are OCR-damaged. GAP-026 says what this needs is document delivery, not
114	another search. **An OCLC number is what converts "find Walter 1971" into "request OCLC 222208".**
115	
116	## 6. New: Elmer 1957, and the literature correcting itself
117	
118	REF-01005 reports that **Elmer (1957) found 1:8 acceptable as a maximum** and then discounts it — his
119	subjects were young, highly trained users at a rehabilitation-education centre, where Walter's sample
120	and Steinfeld's own included large proportions of older people and many with reduced arm function and
121	low stamina. Extraction 57, `contested=1`.
122	
123	That is a **sampling** objection, made in 1979, on exactly the grounds this project would use today.
124	It also dates candidate 110 from a primary source and gives it an author and a form it never had.
125

Adversarial review of research batch 19 (branch claude/next-batch-ngph6l). Findings ranked worst first. Every command is read-only; the DB was opened `mode=ro` throughout. Two things I installed into the container to do the work, neither touching the repo: `pip install pymupdf` (JBIG2 page rendering) and nothing else.

Rendered page images used below are in `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-guidebook/ca1ae452-3545-55f6-8566-12bf9a91f730/scratchpad/` (page55.png, page56.png, page56_lower.png, page162.png, page167_upper.png, page167_lower.png, page168.png, page169.png, page51.png). Downloaded FHWA OCR text is beside them (provisionsforeld00temp*.txt).

---

## F1 — The Templer universal negative is FALSE, and a route the batch used the same hour answers it

**Artefacts:** `sessions/session_2026-09-20-research-batch-19-pre1990-chain-steinfeld-walter-templer.md` §4 lines 70-95; `gaps.GAP-037` amendment clause (2); `search_candidates` 115 notes; `search_executions` 90 `findings_note`; `search_candidates` 117.

**Claim:** "John A. Templer's corpus is stairs end to end", "Four items across fifteen years, not one about ramps", "one of them has no ramp research to his name", "Templer 1977 does not resolve to any indexed item".

**Failure case:** Internet Archive (National Transportation Library collection) holds three volumes of Templer, John A., *Provisions for elderly and handicapped pedestrians: final report*, FHWA-RD-79-1 (Jan 1979), -2 and -3 (May 1980), Georgia Institute of Technology Pedestrian Research Laboratory, contract DOT-FH-11-8504, OCLC 5844243, full OCR text downloadable. Vol 3 (`provisionsforeld00temp_0`) contains a chapter "Studies of short ramps, tactile surfaces and wheelchair dimensions", tables "Gradient Ratings by Manual Wheelchair Users" at 1:5.3 / 1:8 / 1:10.67 / 1:12 / 1:13.3 / 1:16 / 1:20 over 2–10 ft lengths, and Table 20 "Ramp Gradient Recommendations" (1:8, 1:10, 1:12, 1:16 against 3"/6"/9" curb heights). The word "ramp" occurs 1060 times, "1:12" 56 times. Its literature review describes Walter 1971 in detail (adjustable ramp, 20 ft at 1:8.6–1:16 and 10 ft at 1:5.5–1:10; recommends 1:16 at 20 ft self-propelled) and "a more extensive study currently underway at Syracuse University" — i.e. REF-01005. This is ramp research, by the Templer the footnote names, in the transportation-report stratum the batch's own prior P3a pointed at (0.5).

The endpoint that finds it — `archive.org/advancedsearch.php` — is the one the batch used for Walter (W5, `c60a7dee0c49ea6d.json`) at 03:10 the same session; it was never pointed at Templer. Candidate 115's own batch-18 note already recorded "REF-00980's reference list holds Templer J A (1984) *Guidelines for accommodating the handicapped on crossings*" — a pedestrian-crossing item in hand while the batch concluded "no ramp research to his name". The Crossref query that "resolved his corpus" (T6, `cdf823992cae2556.json`) searched the string `Templer stair shape human movement`: a query containing "stair" returning stair papers is not evidence a corpus is stairs; it is the query shape.

Consequences: §4's "the structural finding survives whichever it is" does not survive; candidate 117 stages the wrong neighbour; §13 item 2 sends the next batch to retrieve a stairs report; and §3's "priority of retrieving them drops" is inverted — Table 13's 1:8 row (2 ft projection, 3 in rise) and 1:10 row (8 ft, 9 in) are short-ramp geometry, which is exactly Templer's Table 20 domain. I do not settle which Templer item footnote c means (Vol 3 is dated after REF-01005; the project's field tests ran Jul 1976–Sep 1977); the point is that the class of item the batch declared non-existent exists in full text on an open route.

```
curl -sS 'https://archive.org/advancedsearch.php?q=creator%3ATempler+AND+%28pedestrian+OR+ramp+OR+handicapped%29&fl%5B%5D=identifier&fl%5B%5D=title&fl%5B%5D=year&rows=20&output=json'
curl -sS -L https://archive.org/download/provisionsforeld00temp_0/provisionsforeld00temp_0_djvu.txt | grep -ciE '\bramp'
curl -sS -L https://archive.org/download/provisionsforeld00temp_0/provisionsforeld00temp_0_djvu.txt | grep -oE '.{200}Table 20 Ramp Gradient Recommendations.{300}'
```

## F2 — The transcription describes the OCR TEXT LAYER, not the scan, and the scan is legible

**Artefact:** `retrieval-log/session_2026-09-20-research-batch-19-pre1990-chain-steinfeld-walter-templer/08263082ebdda8eb.json` (`ocr_damage_note`, per-entry `note`s); session §2, §5; candidates 116, 120, 122; extraction 57 notes; attestation `source-discipline` reason.

**Claim:** "no OCR engine is available in this environment … so this text layer is the best that exists here"; entries marked "[author illegible]", "AUTHOR LOST TO THE SCAN", "'Ramps' IS NOT [legible]", "Year OCR reads '194-5/' and is NOT resolvable to 1957", "the bibliography's own year digits for Walter are OCR-damaged", "an initial that is NOT an F on its face".

**Failure case:** the pages are JBIG2 images inside the PDF; `pip install pymupdf` renders them in seconds and the Read tool displays them. Rendered at 110–150 dpi, pages 167–169 read plainly. Against the artefact:
- "Birren, J.E. Psychology of aging. Englewood Cliffs, NJ: Prentice Hall, 1964" → transcribed "[Cu]rren", alpha_position "C", plus a bogus note that Brattgard is "out of strict order in the scan". The scan is in strict order: ANSI, AT&T, Birren, Brattgard, Churchman…
- "Corlett, E.N., Hutcheson, C., DeLugan, M.A. and Rogozenski, J. Ramps or stairs, in Applied ergonomics, 3:4, pp 195-201, 1972" → "Ramps" is legible; the artefact says it is NOT and scores it ceiling-only, so the reported slope-strict floor of 1 is wrong (floor is 2: Elmer + Corlett). Candidate 116's "THE TITLE MAY NOT CONTAIN 'Ramps' AT ALL" is false.
- "Elmer, C.D. … Ph.D. dissertation, University of IL, 1957" → year legible; artefact and extraction 57 say it is not.
- "Jones, J.C. Fitting for action" → "[author illegible] AUTHOR LOST TO THE SCAN". "Kidwell, A.M." → "K[?], O.M.". "Kira, A." → "[author illegible]". "Nichols, P.J.R." → "[surname illegible]". "Harrigan, J.E." → "Harri[m]an". "Steinfeld, Edward" → "Eckard" recorded as the reading. ANSI "1961 (R1971)" → "19[6]?". "American Telephone and Telegraph Co. … 1975" → "unresolved".
- "Walter, F. … London: Disabled Living Foundation, 1971" → session §5 says the year is unreadable and candidate 120 builds a whole "unexplained initial" trail on "rE". It is an F and a 1971.
- "Templer, J.A. … New York: Columbia University, 1974" → "[?] [Un]iversity".
- JSON entry order puts Thiberg before Templer; the scan has Templer first, and the artefact's own `completeness` field says its order is "derived from the ordering in the document".

The floor/ceiling "band" added to `scripts/research/mining_screen.py` measures the distance between a damaged text layer and a guess, when the source of truth was one render away. The attestation's "where the OCR gives … an author initial that is not an F, nothing is repaired from memory" praises leaving visible a damage that the document does not have.

What survives: a letter-multiset diff of `unstructured` against `ocr_verbatim` finds NO letters added in any of the 38 entries (only drops), so the conservative band did not smuggle; Elmer's "ramp" is in the OCR bytes; the count of 38 is right; the ANSI→Webb alphabetical span is unbroken and page 169 ends in the GPO imprint, so the span-completeness claim holds.

```
pip install pymupdf
python3 -c "import pymupdf; d=pymupdf.open('retrieval-log/session_2026-09-18-research-batch-18-archive-route-ramp-threshold/5dd866a236fb5978.pdf'); [d[i].get_pixmap(dpi=120).save(f'/tmp/p{i}.png') for i in (167,168,169)]"
# then view /tmp/p167.png etc. with the Read tool
```

## F3 — The footnote-scope reading SURVIVES; what is built on it does not

**Artefacts:** session §3; extraction 56 (`source_value_extractions` 56); GAP-037 amendment clause (1).

**Survives:** page index 56 rendered (`page56_lower.png`) shows a superscript `c` on the 1:8 and 1:10 rows and none on 1:12 or 1:16; footnote c reads "Based on research of others". Page index 55 (Table 12) and the procedure text on printed p.49 confirm the study stepped 1:12 → 1:16 → 1:20 only. Not OCR noise; the pattern of trailing single letters (`Rampveysa`, `(in feet)b`, `steepc`) is consistent superscript rendering.

**Failures:**
(a) The footnote reads "(Templer, 1977 and **Walters**, 1971)". Extraction 56's `claim_text` normalises it to "Walter" and its note attributes the difference to OCR damage ("the OCR damage is on 'Walter'"). The OCR `WaJter$` was reading a real `s`. The report is internally inconsistent (Walters in the footnote, Walter in the bibliography); the extraction erases the source's own variance and files it as scan damage.
(b) "A cleaner copy of page 57 decides it in one look" — the existing copy decides it; nobody looked. And "page 57" is the 1-based PDF page; the printed page is 54. A reader with a physical copy is sent to the wrong page. Same convention on extraction 57 (`loc_section` 163 = PDF page; printed 161).
(c) The inference "the 1:12 and 1:16 rows rest on Steinfeld's own data" over-reads the absence of a marker. The report's own comparison section (printed p.161, `page162.png`) says "Walter's findings for ramps are similar to ours. Both studies found a 1:16 slope for 20 feet to be accessible to at least 95 percent of the wheelchair users." Walter is, by the report's own words, corroboration for the 1:16 row. The amendment's "Templer and Walter are not nodes of the 1:12 chain at all, and the priority of retrieving them drops" contradicts GAP-037 clause (5), which the same amendment says "STANDS UNCHANGED".
(d) Given F1, the two `c`-marked rows are the short-ramp bands, which points AT Templer's curb-ramp work, not away from it.

## F1 — The Templer universal negative is FALSE, and a route the batch used the same hour answers it

**Artefacts:** `sessions/session_2026-09-20-research-batch-19-pre1990-chain-steinfeld-walter-templer.md` §4 lines 70-95; `gaps.GAP-037` amendment clause (2); `search_candidates` 115 notes; `search_executions` 90 `findings_note`; `search_candidates` 117.

**Claim:** "John A. Templer's corpus is stairs end to end", "Four items across fifteen years, not one about ramps", "one of them has no ramp research to his name", "Templer 1977 does not resolve to any indexed item".

**Failure case:** Internet Archive (National Transportation Library collection) holds three volumes of Templer, John A., *Provisions for elderly and handicapped pedestrians: final report*, FHWA-RD-79-1 (Jan 1979), -2 and -3 (May 1980), Georgia Institute of Technology Pedestrian Research Laboratory, contract DOT-FH-11-8504, OCLC 5844243, full OCR text downloadable. Vol 3 (`provisionsforeld00temp_0`) contains a chapter "Studies of short ramps, tactile surfaces and wheelchair dimensions", tables "Gradient Ratings by Manual Wheelchair Users" at 1:5.3 / 1:8 / 1:10.67 / 1:12 / 1:13.3 / 1:16 / 1:20 over 2–10 ft lengths, and Table 20 "Ramp Gradient Recommendations" (1:8, 1:10, 1:12, 1:16 against 3"/6"/9" curb heights). The word "ramp" occurs 1060 times, "1:12" 56 times. Its literature review describes Walter 1971 in detail (adjustable ramp, 20 ft at 1:8.6–1:16 and 10 ft at 1:5.5–1:10; recommends 1:16 at 20 ft self-propelled) and "a more extensive study currently underway at Syracuse University" — i.e. REF-01005. This is ramp research, by the Templer the footnote names, in the transportation-report stratum the batch's own prior P3a pointed at (0.5).

The endpoint that finds it — `archive.org/advancedsearch.php` — is the one the batch used for Walter (W5, `c60a7dee0c49ea6d.json`) at 03:10 the same session; it was never pointed at Templer. Candidate 115's own batch-18 note already recorded "REF-00980's reference list holds Templer J A (1984) *Guidelines for accommodating the handicapped on crossings*" — a pedestrian-crossing item in hand while the batch concluded "no ramp research to his name". The Crossref query that "resolved his corpus" (T6, `cdf823992cae2556.json`) searched the string `Templer stair shape human movement`: a query containing "stair" returning stair papers is not evidence a corpus is stairs; it is the query shape.

Consequences: §4's "the structural finding survives whichever it is" does not survive; candidate 117 stages the wrong neighbour; §13 item 2 sends the next batch to retrieve a stairs report; and §3's "priority of retrieving them drops" is inverted — Table 13's 1:8 row (2 ft projection, 3 in rise) and 1:10 row (8 ft, 9 in) are short-ramp geometry, which is exactly Templer's Table 20 domain. I do not settle which Templer item footnote c means (Vol 3 is dated after REF-01005; the project's field tests ran Jul 1976–Sep 1977); the point is that the class of item the batch declared non-existent exists in full text on an open route.
